explanation: Compared with Karpenko, 'Fields of any u-invariant but a 2-power minus 1 or 3' (preprint, rev. Nov 2026), whose introduction summarises: the u-invariant is the highest dimension of a non-degenerate anisotropic quadratic form; the possible finite values start with 1, exclude 3, 5, 7, include all 2-powers (Kaplansky 1953; Lam Ch. XI §6), all positive even integers (Merkurjev), 9 (Izhboldin) and 2^r+1 (Vishik); Theorem 1.1 gives every u not of the form 2^r-1 or 2^r-3. IsUInvariant n says some char ≠ 2 field F : Type has n as the greatest element of anisotropicDims F (dimensions of nondegenerate anisotropic forms on F^n), the standard definition; the universe restriction is justified by Löwenheim–Skolem as the docstring explains. This declaration asks whether 13 = 2^4 - 3 is a u-invariant, the smallest case of the form 2^r - 3 not covered by Karpenko's Theorem 1.1. Faithful.
